claim.claim-text: 1. A method comprising:
wherein the student training data includes information related to results of virtual reality destructive testing.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the student performs the virtual welding process on a welding coupon using a mock welding tool.
3. The method of claim 1 or 2, further comprising using the LMSA to select graded joint configurations from a list to create a grade book for a class.

4. The method of one of the claims 1 to 3, further comprising using the LMSA to enter welding projects and assignments, that are not derived directly from the virtual reality welding system, for data manipulation.
5. The method of one of the claims 1 to 4, further comprising using the LMSA to apply pricing to the student training data to determine a cost savings.
6. The method of one of the claims 1 to 5, further comprising using the LMSA to organize training data for a plurality of students by one or more of class, period, or shift.
7. The method of one of the claims 1 to 6, further comprising using the LMSA to measure improvement by the student between two welding exercises or points in time.
8. The method of one of the claims 1 to 7, further comprising using the LMSA to generate pass/fail indications based on a cutoff score input by a welding instructor.
9. The method of one of the claims 1 to 8, further comprising using the LMSA to add performance comments to a report for the student.

10. The method of one of the claims 1 to 9, further comprising using the LMSA to generate a report card and select items to be included or excluded from the report card for the student; and/or further comprising using the LMSA to generate printable reports by one or more of a welding student, a welding class, or a time frame.
11. The method of one of the claims 1 to 10, further comprising using the LMSA to archive final welding class results to the database server system.

12. The method of one of the claims 1 to 11, further comprising using the LMSA to create and track virtual certifications as acquired by the student performing to determined levels on welding exercises.

13. The method of one of the claims 1 to 12, further comprising: using the LMSA to enter real-world welding data generated during a real-world welding process performed by the student using a real-world welding machine; and using the LMSA to compare the real-world welding data to at least a portion of the student training data associated with the student.

14. A learning management system (100) comprising: a virtual reality welding system (1400) configured to generate student training data in response to a student performing at least one virtual welding process on the virtual reality welding system (1400); characterized by:

a database server system configured to receive and store the student training data; and a personal computer having a learning management software application (LMSA) installed thereon, wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) comprises executable computer instructions configured to execute on the personal computer to perform each of:

the learning management system further preferably comprising an external communication infrastructure (1710), preferably including one or more of the internet, a cellular communication network, a WiFi communication network, or a satellite communication network; and/or wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) preferably further comprises executable computer instructions configured to execute on the personal computer to analyze the student training data and generate the analysis results and the reports; and/or wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) preferably further comprises executable computer instructions configured to generate at least one grade for at least one welding student based on at least a portion of the student training data; and/or wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) preferably further comprises executable computer instructions configured to identify, based on at least a portion of the student training data, any welding skills that a welding student is having trouble mastering; andor wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) preferably further comprises executable computer instructions configured to compare welding performance of two or more welding students based on at least a portion of the student training data; and/or wherein the learning management software application (LMSA) preferably provides instructional welding lessons and materials for one or more of welding students and welding instructors; and/or wherein the student training data preferably includes information related to welding parameters including at least one of contact tip to work distance, weld angle, travel angle, and travel speed as affected by a welding student during a virtual welding process; and/or wherein the student training data includes information related to at least one of a welding student name, a date and time of a virtual welding process performed by a welding student, default tolerances used during a virtual welding process, technique parameter scores based on a welding procedure specification (WPS), a welding pass number and a weld score per pass, an average of weld score passes, an overall score, a welding process and technique used, a joint configuration and position, discontinuities and percent, number of welds completed per joint configuration, data for return-on-investment reporting, student arc time, student material usage, and student simulator time.

15. The method according to one of the claims 1 to 13, characterized by: accessing a database server system using a personal computer having a learning management software application (LMSA) installed thereon; downloading student training data from the database server system to the personal computer using the LMSA, wherein the student training data derives from one or more virtual welding processes performed on one or more virtual reality welding systems; and analyzing the student training data using the LMSA to determine a welding performance of one or more welding students associated with the student training data;

further preferably comprising using the LMSA to select graded joint configurations from a list to create a grade book for a class; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to enter welding projects and assignments, that are not derived directly from a virtual reality welding system, for data manipulation; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to apply pricing to data to determine a cost savings; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to organize student data by one or more of class, period, or shift; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to measure student improvement between two welding exercises or points in time; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to generate pass/fail indications based on a cutoff score input by a welding instructor; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to add performance comments to a report for a welding student; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to generate a report card and select items to be included or excluded from the report card for a welding student; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to generate printable reports by one or more of welding student, welding class, or time frame; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to archive final welding class results to the database server system; and/or further preferably comprising using the LMSA to create and track virtual certifications as acquired by welding students performing to determined levels on welding exercises; and/or further preferably comprising: using the LMSA to enter real world welding data generated during a real-world welding process performed by a first student welder using a real-world welding machine; and using the LMSA to compare the real-world welding data to at least a portion of the student training data associated with the first student welder.
